stemMd: The student wants to explain to an audience unfamiliar with the topic how an anagama kiln produces the glaze on its pots. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Because ash falls unevenly inside the chamber, no two pots from a single anagama firing come out alike.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Junko Mori, who fires an anagama kiln twice a year in Oregon, says that the kiln, not the potter, decides a pot's surface.

options.label: C
options.textMd: In an anagama kiln, wood burns continuously for days, and the ash it throws off settles on the pots and melts into a glaze.

options.label: D
options.textMd: An anagama kiln is a single-chamber wood-fired kiln built along a slope, and a single firing lasts several days.

explanationMd:
A rhetorical synthesis question is scored against the stated goal, not against how interesting the sentence is. Here the goal has two parts: explain the glaze, and do it for someone new to the topic.

That means the sentence must trace the glaze back to its cause. Only Choice C does: wood burns, ash flies, ash lands on the pots, ash melts into a glaze. It uses two notes (continuous firing and ash melting into glaze) and needs no prior knowledge to follow.

Check a synthesis answer by asking whether a reader who knew nothing could answer the goal's question after reading only that sentence. "How is the glaze made?" is answered by Choice C alone. The other three sentences are all accurate uses of the notes, but a reader would finish them still not knowing where the glaze comes from.

distractorRationale.b: This uses the quotation and the biographical note, which speak to who controls the outcome rather than to how the glaze forms. A reader new to the topic would learn nothing about ash or melting.
distractorRationale.d: This describes the kiln's construction and the length of a firing but stops before the glaze. It is relevant background, not an explanation of the process the goal names.
distractorRationale.a: This states a consequence of the process — that every pot differs — rather than the process itself. It presupposes the ash-and-glaze mechanism that the goal asks the student to spell out.

accessibilityText: Using the six student notes about anagama kilns, choose the sentence that best explains to a newcomer how the kiln produces the glaze on its pots.

provenance.notes: Original item. Every option is a faithful use of the notes, so the item turns on which one meets the stated rhetorical goal.

review.author: digital-sat-wave3-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The goal is explaining how the glaze is produced; only c states the mechanism (continuous wood fire -> ash settles on pots -> melts into glaze). d defines the kiln without mentioning glaze.

review.notes: Author solved and checked uniqueness: only C supplies the causal chain from burning wood to melted ash glaze; A, B and D are accurate but answer a different question. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
